Archived 2026-08-28 as openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-28-auditoria-sombra-lead-capture-investigation. Investigation-only (no code changed), Subdomain 2 of the freemium-onboarding master plan. Question: does completing Auditoria Sombra leave a queryable lead trace before a discovery call is booked? Answer: depends on the layer — apps/backend's run_auditoria_sombra (wizard_service.py) is genuinely stateless (verified by direct reading + 3-way adversarial verification + independent reviewer re-check), but the real-world caller, the contexia-wizard Next.js app, DOES persist: Step8Diagnostico.tsx unconditionally calls its own /wizard/api/audit/execute route, which writes audit_result/audit_executed_at/status/lead_score to Supabase `leads` and fires an internal Resend notification. Net: no lead is silently lost today. Implication for Subdomain 5 (freemium-tenant-minimum-seed): don't build persistence that already exists — first confirm whether the freemium entry point is contexia-wizard (covered) or a new direct-backend surface (would need its own write path). Also flagged: CentinelaService.save_alerts() is never called by this flow (raw alerts never persisted, only the LLM-merged summary), and two unrelated features share the 'Auditoria Sombra' name in this repo (the GTM wizard vs. a tenant-facing PDF/HITL report generator) — Subdomain 3's plan-tier gating must not conflate them. Reviewed via reviewer subagent: CHANGES_REQUESTED (one wrong line-range citation, one missing footnote), both fixed, findings otherwise fully verified against live code. Full findings note: openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-28-auditoria-sombra-lead-capture-investigation/reports/2026-08-28-findings.md. No Stage 11 (nothing to deploy).

Archived 2026-08-28 as openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-28-chatwoot-b2b-lead-capture-investigation. Investigation-only (no code changed), additional subdomain prompted by a founder question comparing Chatwoot's importance to HubSpot's. Question: does a Campana-2-eligible (B2B SaaS) prospect who first messages Taty on WhatsApp (Chatwoot, confirmed live/running at localhost:3020) ever get captured/flagged as a B2B lead? Answer: no. taty_lead_router.py::classify_lead_intent() has exactly 3 outcomes (sales_interest/payment_confirmation/unknown), all B2C-Renta-Natural-scoped; the nearest signal (obligado_declarar) is a Renta Natural filing-threshold check, not a UVT-crossing/persona-juridica classifier, and drives no branch anyway; crm_leads has no business-type column and zero code path connects it to tenants/b2b_clients creation; the Chatwoot custom-attribute schema (chatwoot-mcp-and-attributes, archived 2026-08-15) DOES define B2B-shaped dropdown values (tipo_contribuyente: SAS, servicio_interes: creacion_empresa/CFO) but the auto-tagging pipeline that would populate them was explicitly deferred as a fast-follow and never built — SAS is structurally unreachable by the actual _auto_tag_chatwoot() code, which only maps 2 intents + 1 boolean; HubSpot sync is hardcoded to one free-tier Deal pipeline, incapable of routing differently. Reviewer found and added corroborating evidence not in the original research: apps/chatwoot-bridge/main.py:177 hardcodes tipo_lead='b2c_whatsapp' on every new WhatsApp contact. Net: only a human operator manually reading Chatwoot could surface such a lead today — nothing systematic exists. Informs Subdomain 4 (crm-alta-tiered-provisioning): WhatsApp is not a source of B2B leads today, automated or otherwise. Reviewed via reviewer subagent: APPROVED, all claims independently re-verified against live code plus an independent repo-wide grep for missed bridges (none found). Full findings note: openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-28-chatwoot-b2b-lead-capture-investigation/reports/2026-08-28-findings.md. No Stage 11 (nothing to deploy).
